newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker as U.S. market softens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker as U.S. market softens.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in quiet trade on Monday, taking their cue from a drop in U.S. Treasury prices, with investors looking ahead to testimony this week by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, dealers said.

"I think we're largely following (the U.S. drop). There's no new news for Canada," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc. "It was very quiet overnight and it looks pretty quiet here right now."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.65 to C$112.27 to yield 6.973 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 14/32 to yield 6.67 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 30 basis points from 28 basis points at Friday's close.

Weakness in U.S. Treasuries is being caused largely by a softer U.S. dollar, which is prompting many foreign investors to take profits, said Webber. That weakness, in turn, is spilling over into Canada.

Analysts said activity was subdued in both markets with many players sidelined until U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivers his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday and Thursday. Many investors are expecting Greenspan to offer hints about the near-term direction of U.S. rates.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.45 to C$104.85 to yield 6.324 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.40 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to eight basis points from 11 basis points on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.90 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.11 percent.
